sections.lede: Your 3D models deserve better. Whether it's a photogrammetry scan, a game asset, or your logotype extruded into a mesh — inspect it, present it, export it without ever leaving the tab. Capture your assets the way they were meant to be seen, ready for your website, portfolio or next presentation.

sections.title:
Goes a lot deeper
than you think
sections.lede: It's not just a viewer. It's a studio. UV checker, wireframe, clay mode, isometric camera, ColorChecker, onset reference kit, a dynamic curved studio backdrop — and the list goes on. The kind of tooling you'd expect from a desktop app, running quietly in your browser tab.

cards.title: Light Control
cards.body: Key, fill, and rim — a full studio rig ready in seconds. Per-light intensity, height, and rotation, with orbit and shadow control built in.

cards.title: Mesh Diagnostics
cards.body: UV checker, wireframe overlay, and clay mode. Everything you need to sanity-check your mesh without opening a DCC.

cards.title: Animation Preview
cards.body: Rigged clips, baked cycles, and timeline scrub. Everything you need to preview motion before you export — no DCC required.

cards.title: Custom HDRI
cards.body: Drop your own 2:1 environment — HDR, EXR, JPG, or PNG — and light your model with your studio, location, or client asset. Same controls as the built-in library. Nothing leaves your machine.

cards.title: Spotlight Gobos
cards.body: Palm, leaf, and tree gobos on the key light — dappled shadows and instant mood. Softness, scale, and rotation without a single flag.

cards.title: Isometric Camera
cards.body: Switch to isometric view, step 45° around your model, and export 2D game assets exactly as they'll appear in your world.

cards.title: Look Filters
cards.body: Cinematic presets, luminance curve, and full color grade — everything you need to land the mood before export. No round trip through Lightroom.

cards.title: Lens Effects
cards.body: Lens flare, dirt, and chromatic aberration — optical polish on your hero without a post round trip. Dial intensity, color, and quality in realtime.

cards.title: Color Reference
cards.body: Reference spheres, ColorChecker, lit/unlit toggle — everything you need to validate your grade and match your CG to the real world.

sections.title: Roadmap
sections.lede: A lot is already here. A lot more is coming. Features get added, timelines shift, and we're always building — but this is our best outline of what's next and when to expect it.

faq.question: Who is Orby for?
faq.answer: Orby is built for 3D artists who need a fast, clean view without booting up a full DCC — and for designers who need to present 3D content without a pipeline. AI-generated models, product visuals, client presentations, logo extrusions. No setup, no commitment. Just your file and an instant virtual studio.

faq.question: Do I need to create an account?
faq.answer: No. No account, no login, no email, no waitlist. Just open the browser and drop your file. We wanted getting started to be as frictionless as possible — no hoops, no setup, no commitment. If you have a file, you're ready.

faq.question: Do my files get uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: Never. Orby runs entirely in your browser — your files don't leave your device, ever. No servers, no cloud, no storage. Close the tab and the model is gone. What you load stays yours.

faq.question: What formats does Orby support?
faq.answer: Orby is built and optimized for GLB and glTF — that's where you'll get the full experience. It also supports OBJ, FBX, STL, and USD/USDZ with basic support. For best results, export as GLB.

faq.question: Can I export my renders?
faq.answer: Yes. You can export stills and video without leaving the tab. What you see is what you get — post-processing, lighting, materials and all.

faq.question: Does it work on mobile?
faq.answer: Not yet. Orby is built for desktop — a proper screen, a mouse, and some GPU headroom. Mobile support is on the roadmap, but for now leave it at your desk.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Completely. No hidden tiers, no export limits, no watermarks. Free now, free always.

faq.question: Why does Orby exist?
faq.answer: Orby started as a personal learning experiment — I wanted to learn more about code and 3D on the web, and the process of building something on my own. It was never meant to be anything more than that. But it kept growing, and at some point it became something worth sharing. So here it is. I hope it's useful.

sections.lede: rfrct is a design tool for distorting type and building audio-reactive visuals, right in the browser. Bend your letters through glass, push them through waves, blur the edges until they frost over. Dial in chromatic aberration, layer on refraction, and let the whole thing react to sound. When you're done, export it as a PNG, a GIF, or straight to MP4 — no plugins, no timelines, no fuss. Early access is limited.
